objects: A real inner-product space E; a nonempty finite index type κ; a population continuous linear operator Σ : E →L[ℝ] E; a sample x : κ → E; a real bound B; the empirical second-moment operator M̂; and the centered summands x_i ⊗ x_i − Σ.
domains: B is real; x_i lies in E; Σ, M̂, x_i ⊗ x_i, and x_i ⊗ x_i − Σ are continuous linear endomorphisms of E over ℝ.
quantifiers: For every nonempty finite type κ, every continuous linear operator Σ, every sample x : κ → E, every real B, and every i ∈ κ, subject to the stated hypotheses.
assumptions: B ≥ 0; Σ is symmetric; ‖Σ‖ ≤ B²; and ‖x_i‖ ≤ B for every i ∈ κ.
conclusion: The empirical deviation equals the average of the centered rank-one summands; every centered summand is symmetric; and every centered summand satisfies ‖x_i ⊗ x_i − Σ‖ ≤ 2B².
scopes: All sums and occurrences of i range over κ. Symmetry is asserted for the underlying real linear maps, while norms and subtraction are those of continuous linear maps E →L[ℝ] E.
constant_dependencies: The numerical factor 2 is universal. The bound depends only on B and is independent of i, |κ|, E, the sample, and Σ once the assumptions hold.
